saa-ini-181.text: A company has a set of instances EC2 Rolling 24/7, with a stable and predictable use profile for the next few years 1 a 3 The team wants to significantly reduce the cost of these instances compared to the On-Demand price, in exchange for a commitment to use for a fixed period. EC2 is more suitable for this scenario?
options: On-Demand Mechanisms, paying the standard price per hour without any discount
Spot Instances, which offer the biggest discounts but can be interrupted by AWS with little warning

Reserved Instances (RIs), which offer significant discounts (up to ~75%) in relation to the price On-Demand in exchange for a commitment to use by 1 or 3 years, ideal for stable and predictable workloads
Dedicated Hosts, which offer physical servers dedicated to the client
saa-ini-181.explanation: Correct. Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years, being the ideal choice for stable, predictable and long-term workloads, as database servers that run continuously.
saa-ini-181.hint: Think of the model of precision of the EC2 which offers significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use by 1 or 3 years, ideal for stable and predictable long-term workloads.
optionRationales: Correct. Reserved Instances offer significant discounts in exchange for a commitment to use 1 or 3 years, being the ideal choice for stable, predictable and long-term workloads, as database servers that run continuously.
The Spot Instances offer the biggest discounts, but can be claimed by AWS with little warning — inadequate for database servers that need to run continuously.
The On-Demand model offers no discount for the long-term and predictable use described, leaving significant cost savings on the table.

Dedicated Hosts meet licensing/conformity requirements that require dedicated physical hardware and are usually more expensive—not primarily a cost optimization mechanism for stable workloads in general.

saa-ini-182.text: A company needs to process a large batch of video rendering every night. Processing is divided into thousands of independent tasks, and the system is already prepared to resume a task in another instance if the current instance is interrupted. The team wants to minimize the cost of computing these tasks, even if this means that some instances may be interrupted by AWS occasionally. What model of precision of the EC2 offers the largest discount for this type of work load tolerant to failures and interruptions?
options: Spot Instances, which offer discounts from up to 90% in relation to the price On-Demand, using unused computing capacity of AWS, may be interrupted with prior warning of 2 minutes
On-Demand Mechanisms Auto Scaling
Dedicated Forums, which guarantee physical hardware dedicated to the customer
Reserved Instances of 3 years, which require long-term commitment
saa-ini-182.explanation: Correct. Spot Instances use idle capacity of AWS and offer the largest possible discounts (up to ~90% in relation to On-Demand), being ideal for workloads tolerant to interruptions, such as batch processing distributed in thousands of independent tasks.
saa-ini-182.hint: Think of the model of precision of the EC2 which uses idle capacity of AWS with the largest possible discounts, but which can be interrupted by AWS with little warning — ideal for interrupt-tolerant loads.
optionRationales: Correct. Spot Instances use idle capacity of AWS and offer the largest possible discounts (up to ~90% in relation to On-Demand), being ideal for workloads tolerant to interruptions, such as batch processing distributed in thousands of independent tasks.
A commitment of 3 years doesn't fit well in a batch workload that could be executed intermittently, and RIs don't offer the biggest discounts available for interruption-tolerant loads.
Dedicated Forums meet compliance/insulation needs and are more expensive — they do not represent a cost minimisation choice for batch jobs that are fault-tolerant.
The On-Demand price offers no special discount — it does not minimize the cost for workloads that can tolerate interruptions, such as Spot Instances allow.

saa-ini-183.text: A company stores audit logs in Amazon S3 which need to be retained by 7 years by regulatory requirement, but rarely (or never) are accessed after the first 90 days. Currently, all logs remain in the storage class S3 Standard, generating high storage costs over the years. S3 allows you to automatically move these objects to a cheaper storage class after a certain period without manual intervention?
options: Manually move objects to another bucket every month
Reduce the number of replicas of the bucket
Lifecycle policy (lifecycle policy) S3, that automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes (such as S3 Glacier) after a defined number of days, according to the expected access pattern
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration in Bucket
saa-ini-183.explanation: Correct. A life cycle policy of the S3 allows you to set rules that automatically transition objects to cheaper storage classes, such as S3 Glacier, after a defined number of days — suitable for long retention and rare access data, without manual intervention.
saa-ini-183.hint: Think about the configuration of S3 automatically moving objects to cheaper storage classes (such as Glacier) after a defined number of days without manual intervention.
optionRationales: Correct. A life cycle policy of the S3 allows you to set rules that automatically transition objects to cheaper storage classes, such as S3 Glacier, after a defined number of days — suitable for long retention and rare access data, without manual intervention.
This is a manual process, subject to errors and operationally costly, compared to an automated life cycle policy.
Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads/downloads in long distances — has no relation to storage class costs.
The S3 does not expose a 'number of replicas' configuration for the customer to reduce; the storage cost is determined by the storage class, not by a replica configuration.

saa-ini-184.text: A company stores millions of objects in S3 whose access patterns are unpredictable and vary over time: some objects are accessed frequently for weeks and then run out of access for months, without a defined standard. The team wants to optimize storage costs automatically, moving objects between frequent and infrequent access levels based on the actual pattern of use, without defining life-cycle rules based on fixed time and without recovery rates to access data at frequent/infrequent levels. S3 meets this requirement?
options: S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access), configured for all objects
S3 Glacier Deep Archive, configured for all objects

S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which monitors access patterns and automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archiving), optimizing costs without impact of performance or recovery rates at these levels
S3 One Zone-IA, configured for all objects
saa-ini-184.explanation: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access patterns of each object and automatically moves it between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archival levels) based on actual use, without charging recovery rates at these levels and without requiring fixed-time life-cycle rules.
saa-ini-184.hint: Think about the storage class of S3 which monitors the patterns of access to objects and moves automatically between cost levels, without the need to define life-cycle rules based on fixed time.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors the access patterns of each object and automatically moves it between frequent and infrequent access levels (and optionally archival levels) based on actual use, without charging recovery rates at these levels and without requiring fixed-time life-cycle rules.

The S3 Standard-IA charges a recovery rate and assumes uncommon access; if some objects are accessed frequently, this would generate high recovery costs — Intelligent-Tiering automatically adapts without these rates at frequent/unreserved levels.
One Zone-IA stores data in a single area of availability (less durability against loss of AZ), still collects recovery fees and does not automatically adapt to unpredictable access patterns.
Glacier Deep Archive has recovery times measured in hours, being inadequate for objects that may need frequent access for weeks.

saa-ini-185.text: The financial team of a company wants to visualize and analyse the expenditure of AWS over time, identify which services or accounts are consuming more financial resources, compare costs between periods and generate future spending forecasts based on usage history. AWS provides this visualization and analysis of historical costs and forecasts?
options: AWS Budgets, only sends alerts when a defined expenditure limit is reached or foreseen
AWS Trusted Advisor, focusing on recommendations for good practice
AWS Billing Console, showing only the current month's bill
AWS Cost Explorer, which allows to visualize and analyze patterns of expenditure and use of AWS over time, with service/account/tag filters, and generate future cost forecasts based on history
saa-ini-185.explanation: Correct. AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive visualizations of expenditures and usage over time, with detailed filters by service, account, tag, among others, besides generating future cost forecasts based on historical data.
saa-ini-185.hint: Think of the service of AWS dedicated to the visualization and interactive analysis of historical expenses, with filters by service/account and generation of future cost forecasts.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive visualizations of expenditures and usage over time, with detailed filters by service, account, tag, among others, besides generating future cost forecasts based on historical data.
The AWS Budgets sends alerts based on defined limits, but the wide historical visualization, detail by service/account and forecasts described are functions of the Cost Explorer.
The Trusted Advisor provides recommendations for good practice in various categories — not designed for interactive historical visualization and cost forecasting.
The collection console shows a summary of the current invoice/coverage — not the capabilities of interactive historical analysis, filters and forecasting of the Cost Explorer.

saa-ini-186.text: A startup with a limited budget wants to be notified automatically by e-mail whenever the monthly expenses of AWS reach 80% of a defined limit, and if again exceeded 100% of this limit, to avoid surprises in the invoice. AWS allows you to set these expense limits and set automatic alerts when they are reached or planned to be reached?
options: AWS Budgets, which allows you to set custom expense limits (budgets) and set automatic alerts by email (or SNS) where actual or projected expenditure reaches defined percentages of the limit
AWS Organizations, configuring expenditure limits per account
Amazon CloudWatch Billing Alarms, with no configuration in AWS Budgets
AWS Cost Explorer, configuring recurring reports
saa-ini-186.explanation: Correct. AWS Budgets allows you to create custom budgets (value, use, RI/Savings Plans) and set up multiple automatic alerts — for example, in 80% and 100% of the limit — sent by e-mail or SNS, based on actual or projected expenditure.
saa-ini-186.hint: Think of the service of AWS dedicated to defining custom expenditure limits and sending automatic alerts when actual or projected expenditure reaches percentages of those limits.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Budgets allows you to create custom budgets (value, use, RI/Savings Plans) and set up multiple automatic alerts — for example, in 80% and 100% of the limit — sent by e-mail or SNS, based on actual or projected expenditure.
The Cost Explorer is focused on historical expense analysis and visualization — does not provide configurable proactive limits-based alerts.

The collection alarms of the CloudWatch support only a single static limit on the total estimated collections, without percentage-based alerts and forecast that the AWS Budgets offers specifically for this case.
The AWS Organizations manages the structure of accounts and policies as SCPs — it does not, by itself, provide expenditure limit alerts; this is the role of the AWS Budgets.

saa-ini-187.text: A new application uses the Amazon DynamoDB, but the team is not sure what the volume of traffic will be in the first few weeks after the launch — it can vary from almost zero to sudden and unpredictable peaks, without a defined standard. The team wants to avoid the risk of providing insufficient reading/writing capacity (causing throttling) or excessive (generating unnecessary cost), preferring to pay only for actual requests made, without having to predict or adjust capacity. DynamoDB meets this initial requirement?
options: On-Demand capacity mode, which charges for reading/writing request performed, climbing instantly to meet unpredictable traffic peaks, without need to provide capacity in advance
Use Amazon RDS in place of the DynamoDB for this case
Capacity Mode Provided with Auto Scaling configured to react only after 1 High time of use
Provisioned Capacity Mode, configured with a high fixed value of RCU/WCU 'for safety'
saa-ini-187.explanation: Right. On-Demand mode of DynamoDB collects only by the reading/writing requirements actually performed and instantly scales to accommodate unpredictable peaks, eliminating the risk of throttling by undersupply or unnecessary cost by oversupply.
saa-ini-187.hint: Think about the capacity mode of the DynamoDB which collects by request performed and instantly scale for traffic peaks, without need to provide capacity in advance.
optionRationales: Right. On-Demand mode of DynamoDB collects only by the reading/writing requirements actually performed and instantly scales to accommodate unpredictable peaks, eliminating the risk of throttling by undersupply or unnecessary cost by oversupply.
Providing a high fixed value 'for safety' leads to paying for unused capacity during low traffic periods — exactly the unnecessary cost that the team wants to avoid.

The Auto Scaling in the provided mode reacts to usage metrics with some delay and is more suitable for loads with at least some basic predictable standard; for a totally unpredictable load, On-Demand avoids both the risk of throttling and the need to manage scaling policies..
Changing the database engine is not related to the capacity modes of the DynamoDB and does not specifically solve the issue of dealing with unpredictable reading/writing traffic in an economic way.

saa-ini-188.text: An application in instances EC2, in private sub-networks, frequently access objects in Amazon S3 through a NAT Gateway (since the private subnet has no direct route to the S3). The volume of data transferred is large, and the team realized that the data processing rates of NAT Gateway they are generating a significant monthly cost only for this traffic destined to S3. Which configuration eliminates this data processing cost from NAT Gateway specifically for traffic with the S3, without compromising the security of the private subnet?
options: Make the sub-network public and assign public IPs to fora
Increase the size (capacity) of NAT Gateway
Compress the data before sending it to S3
Create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3, allowing traffic between the private sub-network and the S3 be routed directly, without going through NAT Gateway and no data processing cost
saa-ini-188.explanation: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3 adds a direct route from the private subnet to the S3 through the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway — eliminating the data processing rate of the NAT Gateway for this traffic, without exposing the sub-network to the internet.
saa-ini-188.hint: Think of the resource of VPC allowing the traffic from a private sub-network to the Amazon S3 be routed directly, without going through NAT Gateway and without generating your data processing rate.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3 adds a direct route from the private subnet to the S3 through the network of the AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway — eliminating the data processing rate of the NAT Gateway for this traffic, without exposing the sub-network to the internet.

The capacity of the NAT Gateway is not configurable in this way and, even if it were, this would not eliminate the data processing rate charged for the traffic intended for S3 — is the wrong mechanism for this problem.
Making the sub-network public exposes the instances to the internet, compromising the security posture of the private sub-network, which the requirement explicitly wants to avoid.

Compression may reduce the volume of data a little bit, but does not eliminate the data collection structure of the NAT Gateway for this traffic — the Gateway Endpoint avoids the NAT Gateway completely for this traffic.

saa-ini-189.text: A company maintains a development environment and tests with several instances EC2 in one Auto Scaling Group. This environment is only used by the team during business hours, Monday to Friday (8h at 19h), and it gets completely idle during nights, early mornings and weekends — but continues to generate cost of instances EC2 Connected 24/7. The team wants to reduce these costs automatically, shutting down instances outside business hours and automatically reconnecting them before the start of the file, without daily manual intervention. EC2 Auto Scaling meets this requirement?
options: Increase the minimum size of the Auto Scaling Group to ensure availability
Scheduled scaling actions, configured to reduce the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling Group (for example: 0) at 19h and restore it before 8h, on weekdays
Target tracking (target tracking) based calibration, configured on the metric of use of CPU
Migrate development environment to Reserved instances
saa-ini-189.explanation: Correct. Scheduled scaling actions allow to define, in advance, recurring times to change the desired capacity of a Auto Scaling Group — reducing it to zero outside business hours and automatically restoring it before the start of the dossier without manual intervention.
saa-ini-189.hint: Think about the type of action of EC2 Auto Scaling which allows to define, in advance, specific times to increase or reduce the desired capacity of a group, on a recurring basis.
optionRationales: Correct. Scheduled scaling actions allow to define, in advance, recurring times to change the desired capacity of a Auto Scaling Group — reducing it to zero outside business hours and automatically restoring it before the start of the dossier without manual intervention.

Target tracking reacts to current load metrics; a leisurely dev environment at night would CPU close to zero, but use-based target tracking would not necessarily reduce capacity to zero following a predictable daily/weekly schedule.
Increasing the minimum size keeps more instances running all the time, increasing the cost instead of reducing it during idle periods.
Reserved Instances commits the continuous payment by capacity (1-3 the opposite of what is needed here..

saa-ini-190.text: After months of operation, a team realizes that its bill of AWS includes volume charges EBS which are no longer attached to any body EC2 (left over from completed instances) and by Elastic IP addresses that are not associated with any running instance. These features do not provide any value, but continue to generate cost. AWS helps to automatically identify this type of idle/unused resource, so that the team can remove it and reduce unnecessary costs?
options: Amazon Macie, identifying sensitive data in S3
Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights, running queries about application logs
AWS Shield, protecting against DDoS attacks
AWS Trusted Advisor, in the category of cost optimization, which identifies resources as volumes EBS not attached and Elastic IPs not associated, helping the team to remove them and reduce costs
saa-ini-190.explanation: Correct. AWS Trusted Advisor, in its cost optimization category, checks the account in search of idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — and recommends removal to reduce unnecessary costs.
saa-ini-190.hint: Think of the service of AWS which, in its cost optimization category, identifies idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — which continue to generate collections.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Trusted Advisor, in its cost optimization category, checks the account in search of idle or unused resources — as volumes EBS Unattached and Unassociated Elastic IPs — and recommends removal to reduce unnecessary costs.
Logs Insights consults application/operation log data — it would neither invent nor signal idle billable resources, such as volumes EBS Unattached or Unassociated Elastic IPs.
The Shield is a protection service against DDoS, not related to the identification of idle/unused resources that generate cost.
The Macie discover and classify sensitive data in S3 — without relation to the identification of idle computing/network resources that generate unnecessary cost.

saa-ini-191.text: A company stores secondary copies of backups in S3 — backups that already exist elsewhere (on-premises) and can be easily regenerated/restored from the primary source if lost. These backups are rarely accessed. The team wants to reduce the cost of storing these secondary backups in S3, accepting a slightly lower level of durability (data stored in a single area of availability), since the loss of this secondary copy would not be critical. S3 offers the lowest cost for infrequent data that do not need redundancy between multiple areas of availability?
options: S3 Glacier Deep Archive, with recovery time up 12 hours
S3 Standard, which stores data redundantly in multiple areas of availability
S3 One Zone-IA (Infrequent Access), which stores data in a single area of availability at a lower cost than the S3 Standard-IA, suitable for secondary or easily recreated data
S3 Standard-IA, which also stores data redundantly in multiple areas of availability
saa-ini-191.explanation: Correct. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one area of availability, offering a lower storage cost than Standard-IA — suitable for secondary copies or data that can be easily recreated if the area is lost.
saa-ini-191.hint: Think about the storage class of S3 which reduces costs by storing data in a single area of availability (rather than multiple), suitable for secondary data that can be recreated if lost.
optionRationales: Correct. S3 One Zone-IA stores data in only one area of availability, offering a lower storage cost than Standard-IA — suitable for secondary copies or data that can be easily recreated if the area is lost.
The S3 Standard offers the highest durability/availability with multi-AZ redundancy, but at a higher cost than is required for easily recreated secondary copies.
Standard-IA offers multi-AZ redundancy with an unusual access price, but One Zone-IA offers an even lower cost for data that does not require multi-AZ redundancy, as described in the scenario.

The recovery times of the Deep Archive (hours) can be very slow depending on the need for recovery, and the question specifically seeks the class that exchanges multi-AZ redundancy at lower cost in infrequent access data — this is the One Zone-IA.

saa-ini-192.text: A company uses instances EC2 of different families and sizes, in addition to functions Lambda and tasks Fargate, and its use of types of instance EC2 changes frequently as the team adopts new generations of instances or migrates workloads between families (e.g. from M5 to M6g). The team wants a commitment of expenses that offers significant discount (similar to Reserved Instances), but that remains applicable regardless of future changes in the family, size, operating system, region or even the computer service used (EC2, Lambda, Fargate). What model of commitment of precision of AWS offers this flexibility?
options: Spot Instances, without any expenditure commitment

Computer Savings Plans, which offer discounts in exchange for a commitment to spend (USD/hour) by 1 or 3 years, automatically applicable to any use of EC2 (any family/size/region/SO), Fargate and Lambda
Reserved Instances Standard RIs, linked to a specific instance type
EC2 Forum Savings Plans, requiring commitment to a family of specific instance in a region
saa-ini-192.explanation: Right. Savings Plans offer discounts in exchange for an hourly expense commitment, automatically applying to the use of computing in any family/size/SO/region of EC2, in addition to Fargate and Lambda — providing the maximum flexibility between the options of Savings Plans.
saa-ini-192.hint: Think of the model of Savings Plans which applies to the use of computing in general (EC2 of any family/size/region, in addition to Fargate and Lambda), instead of restricting oneself to a family of specific instances.
optionRationales: Right. Savings Plans offer discounts in exchange for an hourly expense commitment, automatically applying to the use of computing in any family/size/SO/region of EC2, in addition to Fargate and Lambda — providing the maximum flexibility between the options of Savings Plans.

The EC2 Forum Savings Plans offer slightly higher discounts, but link the commitment to a family of specific instance in a Region — not offering the flexibility between families/regions/services described.
Standard RIs are linked to a specific instance/family/region with limited flexibility for change — the opposite of the flexibility requirement.
The Spot Instances do not involve spending commitment and can be interrupted — do not offer the discount relationship for commitment sought between multiple computing services.
